process.scope: Owns only tapcode.py and tests/test_tapcode.py (both new files). Does not touch bell.py, decimaltime.py, or any existing file; no imports beyond the standard library; no imports from the other two modules.
process.task:
Implement the Tap code (5x5, C/K merged) component exactly to the work order spec, creating only two new files: tapcode.py and tests/test_tapcode.py. Do not modify any existing file; use only the standard library; do not import bell or decimaltime.

Fixed 5x5 table (rows and columns are 1-based): row 1 = A B C D E; row 2 = F G H I J; row 3 = L M N O P; row 4 = Q R S T U; row 5 = V W X Y Z. The table contains no K: K merges with C — encoding K yields C's coordinate (1, 3), and decoding (1, 3) returns "C".

tapcode_encode(text: str) -> list[tuple[int, int]]: preprocess to uppercase, keep only A-Z (K counts as C); each letter yields (row, column). Non-str raises TypeError; empty string returns [].

tapcode_decode(pairs) -> str: pairs must be a list or tuple, each item a (row, col) pair. If pairs itself is not list/tuple (str also rejected) raise TypeError; malformed pair shape or non-int coordinates (bool rejected) raise TypeError; coordinates outside 1–5 raise ValueError. Empty list returns "".

Acceptance examples, every one must have a corresponding test case in tests/test_tapcode.py:
- tapcode_encode("A") == [(1, 1)]
- tapcode_encode("C") == [(1, 3)]
- tapcode_encode("K") == [(1, 3)] (C/K merge)
- tapcode_encode("HELLO") == [(2, 3), (1, 5), (3, 1), (3, 1), (3, 4)]
- tapcode_encode("Z") == [(5, 5)]
- tapcode_encode("") == []
- tapcode_encode("tap code!") == [(4, 4), (1, 1), (3, 5), (1, 3), (3, 4), (1, 4), (1, 5)] (preprocessing: uppercase, non-letters dropped, K→C)
- tapcode_decode([(2, 3), (1, 5), (3, 1), (3, 1), (3, 4)]) == "HELLO"
- tapcode_decode([(1, 3)]) == "C"
- tapcode_decode([]) == ""
- Round-trip: tapcode_decode(tapcode_encode("WORLD")) == "WORLD" and tapcode_decode(tapcode_encode("TAPCODE")) == "TAPCODE"
- tapcode_decode([(0, 3)]), tapcode_decode([(3, 6)]), tapcode_decode([(6, 1)]) each raise ValueError
- tapcode_decode([("1", 3)]), tapcode_decode([(1,)]), tapcode_decode("13"), tapcode_encode(42) each raise TypeError

Include a test case for each acceptance example above (all listed value, round-trip, ValueError and TypeError cases).
